leads.title: Kentucky v. Wasson - Kentucky Supreme Court (1992) / KRS 510.100
leads.documents: Decriminalization of consensual same-sex sexual activity in Kentucky; strikes down sodomy statute that criminalized only same-sex oral/anal contact as misdemeanor.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Kentucky v. Wasson' overturning 'KRS 510.100'; statute 'remains on the books but remains unenforceable'; affirmed by 'Lawrence v. Texas' 2003

leads.title: Bourke v. Beshear (2013) and Love v. Beshear (2014)
leads.documents: Federal challenges to Kentucky's denial of marriage licenses to same-sex couples and refusal to recognize out-of-state same-sex marriages.
leads.detail: Bourke plaintiffs won recognition Feb 12, 2014; Love filed Feb 14, 2014, ruled July 2014 in U.S. District Court in Louisville; Sixth Circuit oral arguments Aug 6, 2014; External links lists 'Bourke v. Beshear, February 12, 2014'

leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges - U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Nationwide legalization of same-sex marriage, striking down Kentucky statutory (since July 1998) and constitutional (Nov 2004 amendment defining marriage as man-woman) bans.
leads.detail: Decision 'handed down on June 26, 2015' requiring states to recognize marriages and issue licenses

leads.title: Executive Order on public employment discrimination - Gov. Steve Beshear June 2008
leads.documents: Bans public-employment discrimination against state workers based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
leads.detail: Originally banned by Gov. Paul Patton 2003 executive order; removed by Gov. Ernie Fletcher 2006; reinstated by Beshear June 2008; Berea Mayor Steve Connelly Feb 2013 order for town's 130 public employees also cited

leads.title: Kentucky Religious Freedom Act of 2013
leads.documents: Creates religious-exemption machinery allowing override of protections; requires state show 'clear and convincing evidence' to infringe 'sincerely held religious beliefs'; risk to local Fairness Ordinances.
leads.detail: Passed March 2013 both houses; supported by Kentucky Family Foundation and Kentucky Catholic Conference; opposed by Kentucky League of Cities, Kentucky Association of Counties, Kentucky ACLU, mayors of Louisville and Covington; Beshear veto overridden 79-15 House and 32-6 Senate

leads.title: EEOC v. R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes - U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
leads.documents: Core transgender-employment protection applicable in Kentucky; Title VII prohibits employment discrimination against transgender people; employers may not use RFRA to justify anti-LGBTQ discrimination.
leads.detail: Ruled March 7, 2018; Sixth Circuit covering Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and Tennessee; facts: Aimee Stephens fired 2013 after disclosing transgender status/transition; boss said 'gender transition violat[es] God's commands'

leads.title: Kentucky hate-crime statutes and Kingdom Come State Park beating prosecution
leads.documents: Enforcement gap: statutes cover hate crimes based on sexual orientation but not gender identity; documents violent anti-gay attack and federal intervention due to lack of local confidence.
leads.detail: March 15, 2012 Kentucky State Police assisted FBI arresting David Jenkins, Anthony Jenkins, Mable Jenkins, and Alexis Jenkins of Partridge for beating of Kevin Pennington April 2011 at Kingdom Come State Park near Cumberland; advocacy by Kentucky Equality Federation president Jordan Palmer lobbying U.S. Attorney for Eastern District of Kentucky Aug 2011

leads.title: Senate Bill 83 (SB83) - 2022 transgender sports ban
leads.documents: Bans transgender athletes from female sports teams; shows override of pro-LGBTQ executive veto.
leads.detail: Passed Kentucky General Assembly March 2022; vetoed by Gov. Andy Beshear April 2022 due to 'constitutionality and legal vagueness concerns'; veto overridden same month, law went into effect immediately

leads.title: House Bill 470 - 2023 ban on gender-affirming care for minors
leads.documents: Criminalizes/prohibits gender-affirming care for minors with no phaseout; enforcement status and protest crackdown relevant to trans visitor safety.
leads.detail: Introduced Feb 2023; House judiciary advanced March 2, 2023, full House passed same day; legislature passed version March 17, 2023; Gov. vetoed; GOP-led legislature overrode March 29 with simple majority; 19 protesters arrested for criminal trespassing; effective July 14, 2023; Sept 28, 2023 federal appeals judges allowed ban to remain pending challenge; Mason-Dixon poll 71% opposed, 21% favor cited

leads.title: Executive Order banning conversion therapy on minors - Gov. Beshear Sept 18, 2024 + city ordinances
leads.documents: Statewide ban on conversion therapy on minors; prior local bans showing patchwork rights machinery.
leads.detail: Illegal since September 18, 2024 when Governor Beshear signed executive order; Covington March 2020 by 5-0, Louisville Sept 2020 by 24-1, Lexington May 2021 unanimous by Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council
